note: Not an index. Dated events in which consciousness, interest or standing was recognised across a species or a substrate boundary. Each entry carries a link. Anyone may propose an addition; the count is the only number here, and it is a count of entries, not a measurement of the world.

events.title: A constitution grants rights to nature
events.text: Ecuador becomes the first country to write rights of nature into its constitution, giving ecosystems standing independent of their usefulness to people.

events.title: A river becomes a legal person
events.text: New Zealand's Te Awa Tupua Act recognises the Whanganui River as a legal person with its own rights, duties and liabilities, ending a claim pursued for more than a century.

events.title: Octopuses, crabs and lobsters recognised as sentient
events.text: Following an independent review of more than 300 studies, the United Kingdom extends its animal sentience legislation to cephalopod molluscs and decapod crustaceans.

events.title: A phonetic structure found in sperm whale calls
events.text: Project CETI and MIT report a combinatorial coda system in sperm whale communication with far more expressive structure than previously described — the first large-scale machine analysis of another species' communication.

events.title: Earth Species Project
events.text: A non-profit building open machine-learning models to decode non-human communication, releasing datasets and models publicly rather than holding them.

events.title: Rewilding Europe
events.text: Land returned to self-regulation across dozens of European landscapes — recognition expressed as ground rather than as language.
